name: Thermal physics states of matter and expansion

questions.q: Which state of matter is characterized by particles that have strong intermolecular forces, vibrate about fixed positions, and maintain a definite shape and volume?
How are particles arranged and how do they move in a liquid compared to a solid?
a: Particles are widely separated and move at high speeds in all directions.
Particles are closely packed but can slide past one another, having no fixed shape.
Particles are held in rigid crystal lattices and cannot move.

questions.q: What term describes the process where a substance changes directly from a solid state to a gas state without passing through the liquid phase?
Which of the following phenomena provides direct experimental evidence of the continuous random motion of particles in a fluid (Brownian motion)?
a: Water boiling in a glass beaker
Metal expanding when heated over a Bunsen burner
Ice melting at zero degrees Celsius
Random jerky motion of smoke particles observed under a microscope when illuminated by light

questions.q: What happens to the internal energy of a substance during a phase change from solid to liquid at its melting point, while temperature remains constant?
a: Internal energy increases as thermal energy is used to break intermolecular bonds.
Internal energy decreases because heat is released.

questions.q: Why does a liquid evaporate even at temperatures well below its boiling point?
a: Only molecules at the exact bottom of the container gain enough heat.
Some faster-moving molecules near the surface possess enough kinetic energy to overcome intermolecular forces and escape into the air.

questions.q: Which of the following factors will decrease the rate of evaporation of a liquid from an open dish?
a: Increasing surface area of the liquid
Decreasing air movement (wind speed) across the surface
Using a liquid with a lower boiling point

questions.q: How does boiling differ from evaporation?
a: Boiling occurs only at room temperature, whereas evaporation happens at high temperatures.
Evaporation only occurs inside closed containers.
Boiling causes the liquid temperature to rise continuously.
Boiling occurs throughout the entire liquid at a fixed temperature, whereas evaporation happens only at the surface across a range of temperatures.

questions.q: When a metal bridge expands on a hot summer day, what structural modification is typically used to prevent buckling or damage?
a: Expansion joints and rollers allowing free movement
Cooling the bridge with refrigerated water pumps
Covering the bridge in thick rubber mats

questions.q: Why does solid expansion occur when a substance is heated?
a: Individual atoms grow larger in physical size.
Increased thermal energy causes particles to vibrate with greater amplitude, increasing the average distance between neighboring particles.
Mass increases as heat is added.

questions.q: Which substance exhibits the highest thermal expansion under normal conditions among common engineering materials?
What is the primary reason why water displays anomalous expansion between 0 degrees Celsius and 4 degrees Celsius?
a: Water molecules decompose into hydrogen and oxygen gases.
Water expands continuously as it gets hotter.
Water has its maximum density at 4 degrees Celsius because ice crystal structures start forming as temperature approaches zero, increasing volume.

questions.q: How does the pressure of a fixed mass of gas in a sealed container change when its temperature is increased at constant volume?
a: Pressure increases because gas molecules gain kinetic energy and collide harder and more frequently with container walls.
Pressure decreases because molecules slow down.

questions.q: What is the absolute zero temperature corresponding to zero thermal energy on the Kelvin temperature scale?
How do you convert a temperature value from degrees Celsius (Celsius) to Kelvin (K)?
a: Add 273 to the Celsius temperature value

questions.q: If a gas in a closed cylinder has its absolute temperature doubled at constant volume, what happens to its pressure?
a: Pressure decreases by a factor of four.

questions.q: What property of a liquid makes it suitable for use in liquid-in-glass clinical or laboratory thermometers?
a: Uniform thermal expansion over a wide temperature range

questions.q: Why is mercury or colored alcohol used in thermometer bulbs instead of water?
a: Water expands anomalously below 4 degrees Celsius and wets glass tubing, making accurate readings difficult.
Water is a solid at room temperature.
Water has zero specific heat capacity.

questions.q: What is meant by the specific latent heat of fusion of a substance?
a: The thermal energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 degree Celsius
The energy released when a gas condenses into a liquid
The thermal energy needed to convert 1 kg of a solid into a liquid at constant temperature
The total energy stored in a chemical bond

questions.q: How much thermal energy is required to melt 2 kg of ice at 0 degrees Celsius, given that the specific latent heat of fusion of ice is 330,000 J/kg?
What term describes the energy required to convert a unit mass of liquid into a gas at its boiling point without any change in temperature?
Why does sweating cool down the human body on a hot day?
a: Sweat adds insulating layers to the skin.
Water molecules with the highest kinetic energy evaporate from the skin surface, leaving behind lower-energy particles and removing thermal energy.
Sweat generates an electrical cooling current.

questions.q: What is the definition of specific heat capacity?
a: The total heat energy stored in an object
The heat required to melt a solid
The energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 degree Celsius
The rate of heat transfer through a material

questions.q: Calculate the thermal energy needed to raise the temperature of 3 kg of water from 20 degrees Celsius to 70 degrees Celsius. (Specific heat capacity of water = 4,200 J/(kg degrees Celsius))
Which of the following states of matter is characterized by ionized atoms and free electrons, existing at extremely high temperatures like in stars?
In a thermocouple thermometer, what physical phenomenon is used to measure temperature?
a: Expansion of mercury in a glass capillary
A voltage produced at the junction of two dissimilar metals when maintained at different temperatures
Change in electrical resistance of a copper wire

questions.q: What happens to the molecules of a gas when the gas is compressed rapidly in a cylinder?
a: Work is done on the gas, increasing its internal energy and raising its temperature.

questions.q: Why do metal pipes carrying steam often include U-shaped expansion loops or bends?
a: To slow down steam flow speed
To allow the metal pipes to expand and contract safely without cracking joints when hot steam passes through

questions.q: What is the primary microscopic difference between boiling and evaporation?
a: Boiling involves bubble formation throughout the liquid volume due to vapor pressure equaling atmospheric pressure, whereas evaporation involves individual surface molecules escaping.
Evaporation occurs only in sealed chambers.

questions.q: If an object has a high specific heat capacity, how does it respond to heating compared to a substance with a low specific heat capacity?
a: It heats up and cools down much faster.
It requires more thermal energy to experience the same temperature rise and heats up more slowly.
It does not expand at all.

questions.q: What is the internal energy of a body defined as?
a: The total kinetic energy of its molecules only
The total potential energy of its molecules only
The total sum of the kinetic and potential energies of all the molecules making up the body
The external mechanical work done on the body

questions.q: Why does a bimetallic strip bend when heated?
a: One metal melts while the other stays solid.
Both metals expand by the exact same amount.
Air pressure pushes harder on one side.
Two different metals have different coefficients of thermal expansion, causing one side to expand more than the other.

questions.q: What is the boiling point of pure water on the Kelvin scale at standard atmospheric pressure?
Which of the following experimental procedures is essential when measuring the specific heat capacity of a metal block using an electric immersion heater?
a: Insulating the metal block to minimize heat loss to the surrounding environment
Placing the block in a block of ice
Stirring the metal block with a glass rod

questions.q: What happens to gas pressure if the volume of a fixed mass of gas is halved at constant temperature (Boyle Law)?
a: Pressure increases by a factor of four.

questions.q: Why do glass tumblers sometimes crack when boiling water is poured into them suddenly?
a: Boiling water reacts chemically with glass.
Uneven thermal expansion occurs because glass is a poor thermal conductor, causing extreme thermal stress between the inner and outer walls.

questions.q: What is the quantity of heat energy released when 0.5 kg of steam condenses to water at 100 degrees Celsius? (Specific latent heat of vaporization = 2,260,000 J/kg)
Why is burns from steam at 100 degrees Celsius often much more severe than burns from boiling water at 100 degrees Celsius?
a: Steam releases an enormous amount of latent heat of vaporization when condensing on the skin in addition to cooling to body temperature.
Steam travels at the speed of sound.
Steam has a lower specific heat capacity.

questions.q: What temperature corresponds to 50 degrees Celsius on the Kelvin scale?
Which of the following best describes Brownian motion?
a: Regular circular orbit of electrons around atomic nuclei
Ordered flow of water molecules in a pipe
Steady diffusion of gases across a room
Random, erratic motion of microscopic dust or pollen suspended in a fluid caused by bombardment from fast-moving invisible fluid molecules
